title: DAXDA Bio-AI & Pharma Protocol: MS Remyelination & Neuro-Regeneration
therapeutic_indication: Relapsing-Remitting & Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS / SPMS)
primary_novel_action: Synergistic dual-target intervention: Ultra-high affinity GPR17 antagonism (18.46 nM Ki at 75.0% receptor occupancy) combined with CN045 nanocatalytic signaling (4.97 µM) and EBV lytic repression (82.1% inhibition).

verified_literature_grounding.title: Longitudinal analysis reveals high prevalence of Epstein-Barr virus associated with multiple sclerosis
verified_literature_grounding.authors: Bjornevik K, Cortese M, Healy BC, et al.
verified_literature_grounding.mechanism: EBV infection increases MS risk 32-fold; viral reactivation drives CD4+ and CD8+ neuro-inflammation.

verified_literature_grounding.title: GPR17 regulates oligodendrocyte differentiation and myelination in the central nervous system
verified_literature_grounding.authors: Chen Y, Wu H, Wang S, et al.
verified_literature_grounding.mechanism: GPR17 acts as an intrinsic timer; down-regulation is essential for OPCs to mature into myelinating oligodendrocytes.

verified_literature_grounding.title: Pharmacological Antagonism of GPR17 Promotes Remyelination in Models of Demyelinating Disease
verified_literature_grounding.authors: Fumagalli M, Lecca D, Abbracchio MP.
verified_literature_grounding.mechanism: Small-molecule antagonism of GPR17 overcomes maturation arrest and restores functional conduction in demyelinated axons.

verified_literature_grounding.title: A Phase 2 Study of Catalytic Nanocrystalline Bioenergetic Agents in Multiple Sclerosis (REPAIR-MS)
verified_literature_grounding.sponsor: Clene Nanomedicine / University of Texas Southwestern
verified_literature_grounding.mechanism: Enhances bioenergetic ATP flux, reduces neurofilament light chain (sNfL), and promotes remyelination kinetics.

verified_literature_grounding.title: Targeting Remyelination and Neuro-Protection in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis
verified_literature_grounding.sponsor: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
verified_literature_grounding.mechanism: Dual-pathway OPC maturation signaling accelerates Visual Evoked Potential (VEP) latency recovery.
